analysis:
Examined both documentation revisions, the binding patch and all supplied metadata against the canonical definition index and selected T-041 detail. NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.swift:224-227 (head) replaces the fixed 8 MiB encoded-body ceiling with maximumEncodedBodyBytes and introduces bodyTooLarge at line 18. Positive-size and 1 MiB template checks remain; the memory quote still scales by 32 times body bytes. The documented 40 MiB ceiling therefore permits a roughly 1.27 GiB header quote rather than roughly 276 MiB, but a larger quote is not itself evidence of an allocation or admission bypass.

The documents consistently describe the owner ceiling (docs/reference/nemotron-super-image-formats.md:94) and a lower HTTP chat-upload ceiling returning 413 (docs/provider/direct-mode.md:261-263). Surrounding documentation retains authentication, pre-decode reservations, pixel/workspace limits, cancellation/drain ownership and qualification caveats. No supplied change alters encryption, credential custody, attestation, serving authorization, billing, cache scope or disk storage; existing retention and local-endpoint sharing are not new findings. Relevant contracts include TB-007, T-010, T-028, T-050 and T-041, with TB-002 governing fleet/local capacity interaction.

No concrete regression is established in this scope. Integration must verify the actual ServingPolicy constant, encodedHeaderQuote callers, enforcement/accounting of the larger quote before JSON/base64/native work, and cleanup on refusal/cancellation in NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.swift. It must also reconcile bodyTooLarge mapping to media_too_large and the outer cap in LocalChatUploadResponder.swift/NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift. Those implementations are not supplied here; documentation is not proof of enforcement. These admission and error-propagation questions are material to the expanded ingress limit.
